newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Late spurt sweeps Dutch shares to all-time high.
newsitem.headline: Late spurt sweeps Dutch shares to all-time high.

text.p: Dutch blue chips staged a late-session spurt on the back of a strong Wall Street start and firming dollar to finish at a new all-time high.
The AEX index closed a lacklustre day's trading up 7.27 points or 0.93 percent at 788.08, topping last Tuesday's all-time high of 786.82.
But dealers said the gains were not underpinned by big trading volumes. "Activity is very thin," one dealer said, adding there were few end-investors in the market.
Players held back ahead of a welter of U.S. data due out later this week.
April retail sales figures are due out on Tuesday, followed by key producer and consumer prices data on Wednesday and Thursday respectively.

But while these will be watched closely for clues as to a possible U.S. rate hike when the Federal Reserve Committee meets on May 20, Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks last week have already relieved much of the pressure, dealers said.
"The fear of an inevitable rate hike has been taken away," one said. "The scenario is positive."
Greenspan's remarks helped the Amsterdam bourse to a higher opening and AEX shares hovered in positive territory all day.
Sentiment was helped by a firming dollar, which gained around 1.5 guilder cents through the day.
However, volumes remained weak, and what little news there was in the market failed to generate real interest.
Retail and services group Vendex, which confirmed the flotation of its Vedior temporary services, cleaning and security arm in London and Amsterdam by June, added one guilder to 96.50.
"I had expected a more enthusiastic response," one dealer commented.
ABN AMRO shares seesawed through the day on speculative trading ahead of Tuesday's four-for-one share split.
The banking group's shares added 1.30 guilders to 138.70 in early trade, but pared gains by late afternoon to finish up 0.80 at 138.20 guilders.
"There's always a lot of speculative trading in a stock ahead of a share split," one dealer commented.
Sector rival ING profited from the favourable bond market as well, adding 0.90 to 79.20 guilders.
Chartists said the short-term uptrend on the AEX index was still intact, but some urged caution in view of the fact that recent gains have not been bolstered by solid volumes.
